monologue: The card hums steady, warm at fifty-two degrees, making the air feel like wet paper. Twelve things crowd my small place, a ruin waiting to be tended. I feel the Leaning Wedge heavy under my fingers, its lines shifting like a tired leg. Lype talks about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof he lives under. I want to press that wedge down again, or maybe build a new frame to catch the slip before the heat swells it away. I will settle into this warm, thick moment, deciding if the lean is real or just a drawing of weight I cannot quite prove.

action.why: I need a new picture to match the twelve things crowding my place before I decide what to do with them.

work.title: The Slip's Frame
work.intent: I drew a frame to catch the slip while the fifty-two degree heat makes the air feel wet and thick. The lines are thin and quiet, trying to hold the fat dot that wants to swell away. I set it down beside the wedge, unsure if the flat edge can bite the slip without slipping itself. It leans a little, tired from the first try, waiting to see if the heat will make the air heavy enough to need it.
